graph_diagnosis.summary: Digital-ad-market share, cost discipline, and AI investment provide limited reusable context.
weaknesses: All earnings, revenue, threshold, analyst-estimate, market-reaction, and outcome links are excluded.
The graph lacks supported engagement, pricing, competition beyond share, or foreign-exchange paths.

search_factors.why_search: Share can support advertiser demand relative to peers.
Cost actions can improve execution but do not prove revenue demand.
AI investment can affect product and ad-performance capacity over time.
Financial performance must be decomposed into independent operating drivers.

checkpoints.mechanism: Improving ad-market share can support advertiser demand.
checkpoints.evidence_requirement: Independent share and advertiser data improve.

checkpoints.mechanism: Cost discipline can support execution but is not a direct revenue driver.
checkpoints.contradiction_signal: Cuts impair product or sales investment.

checkpoints.mechanism: AI investment can improve advertising effectiveness only if adoption and monetization follow.
checkpoints.evidence_requirement: Advertiser performance and adoption indicators improve.

checkpoints.mechanism: Aggregate financial performance is not independent evidence of future revenue acceleration.
checkpoints.evidence_requirement: Separate revenue drivers from profitability and capital allocation.

checkpoints.mechanism: Ad demand, pricing, engagement, competition, and foreign exchange determine revenue-growth acceleration; share, efficiency, and AI are indirect modifiers.
checkpoints.evidence_requirement: Reconcile advertiser demand, pricing, engagement, competition, and FX data.

causal_paths.generalized_mechanism: Share gains can support advertising demand.
Efficiency and AI can modify execution but do not substitute for demand.

alternative_hypotheses.hypothesis: Share gains are insufficient to overcome weak advertiser demand.
alternative_hypotheses.discriminating_evidence: Compare share with ad spending and platform pricing.

forecast_audit_questions: Are ad demand and pricing improving?
Does share translate to advertiser spending?
